name: roblox-cloud-mcp

tools.name: list_experiences
tools.description: List the Roblox experiences this server can read analytics for, with universe IDs, creator, visibility and visit counts. Answers "what games do I have?". No network call — call this first to orient yourself before querying metrics.

tools.name: list_metrics
tools.description: The catalog of every Roblox analytics metric: allowed granularities, valid breakdown dimensions, and data retention window. No network call. Use this before query_metric, or when a query was rejected, to find the exact valid values for a metric.

category.description: Restrict to one family, e.g. "engagement" or "funnel".

metric.description: Show full detail for one metric, including every valid dimension.

search.description: Substring match against metric names and labels.

tools.name: list_dimension_values
tools.description: Discover the actual values of a dimension for one experience — funnel names, custom event names, places, item SKUs. These are defined by the creator’s own game code and cannot be known in advance. Call this before get_funnel or get_custom_event when you do not already know the exact name.

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

range.description: Shorthand date range: "7d", "30d", "yesterday", "today", "last week", "last month", "ytd". Defaults to the last 28 days.

metric.description: The metric providing context, e.g. "FunnelUserTotalCount" or "CustomEventCount".

dimensions.description: Dimensions to list values for, e.g. ["FunnelName"] or ["CustomEventName"].

tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: The "how is my game doing" tool. Active users, sessions, session length and retention over a date range, each with the change against the preceding equal-length period, plus a daily trend. Set detail to "full" to also include day-7 retention, revenue and peak concurrent players. Start here for any general or vague question about an experience.

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

range.description: Shorthand date range: "7d", "30d", "yesterday", "today", "last week", "last month", "ytd". Defaults to the last 28 days.

detail.description: core = active users, sessions, session length, D1 retention (8 API requests). full = adds D7 retention, revenue and peak concurrent players (14 requests, about half the per-minute budget).

tools.name: get_engagement

granularity.description: Bucket size. Defaults per tool. Valid values differ per metric — call list_metrics. Non-cohort funnel metrics support "None" only.

breakdown.description: Dimensions to group by, e.g. ["Platform"] or ["Country"]. Valid dimensions differ per metric — call list_metrics. Note engagement metrics use AgeGroupV2 while funnels, economy and custom events use AgeGroup.

limit.description: Max breakdown series. Only valid with granularity "None" plus a breakdown.

measure.description: activeUsers (DAU) · monthlyActiveUsers · sessions · sessionLength · playtimePerUser · totalPlaytime · stickiness (DAU/MAU).

tools.name: get_experience
tools.description: Read one experience’s settings from Roblox: display name, description, owner, visibility, age rating, which devices players may join from, whether voice chat is on, the private server price, and the root place. This is the live configuration, not analytics.

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

tools.name: list_places
tools.description: List the places inside an experience, with their names, server sizes and how many players are in each right now. Use this to find the place ID for get_place, update_place or restart_servers. (Roblox marks this endpoint beta; it may change.)

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

tools.name: get_place
tools.description: Read one place inside an experience: its name, description, maximum server size, whether it is the root place, and when it was last updated.

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

placeId.description: The place ID. Call list_places if you do not know it.

tools.name: get_experience_config
tools.description: Read one of an experience’s config repositories — the key/value settings the Roblox engine reads at runtime. `view: "published"` (default) is what live servers currently see, `"full"` adds each key’s description and last-modified time, and `"draft"` is the unpublished staging copy plus its draftHash. This tool only reads; there is no config write tool on this server. (Roblox marks this endpoint beta; it may change.)

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

repository.description: Which config repository to read. InExperienceConfig is the general-purpose one; the others configure data stores, leaderboards, recommendations, journeys or anti-cheat.

view.description: published = what live servers see now; full = the same plus per-key descriptions and timestamps; draft = the unpublished staging copy and its draftHash.

tools.name: update_experience
tools.description: Change an experience’s voice chat setting, which devices players may join from, or the private server price. Only the fields you pass are touched — everything else is left exactly as it is. Name, description, visibility and age rating cannot be changed here; they are read-only in this API. Blocking a device stops every player on that platform from joining, and changing the private server price cancels existing private server subscriptions.

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

voiceChatEnabled.description: Turn voice chat on or off. Does not affect servers that are already running.

desktopEnabled.description: Allow players to join from Desktop.

mobileEnabled.description: Allow players to join from Mobile.

tabletEnabled.description: Allow players to join from Tablet.

consoleEnabled.description: Allow players to join from Console.

vrEnabled.description: Allow players to join from VR.

privateServerPriceRobux.description: Monthly private server price in Robux; 0 makes them free, null disables private servers entirely. Either way, every active private server subscription is cancelled. Requires `confirmPriceChange: true`.

confirmPriceChange.description: Must be true to change privateServerPriceRobux. Changing or clearing the private server price cancels every active private server subscription for this experience, and clearing it disables all active private servers. Tell the user before setting it.

tools.name: update_place
tools.description: Change a place’s name, description or maximum server size. Only the fields you pass are touched. Renaming the root place also renames the whole experience. Roblox rejects this with a conflict if the place is open in an active Team Create session.

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

placeId.description: The place ID. Call list_places if you do not know it.

displayName.description: New place name. On the root place this is also the experience name players see.

description.description: New place description. Pass "" to clear it.

serverSize.description: Maximum players per server. Existing servers keep their current size.

tools.name: list_data_stores
tools.description: List the standard data stores in one Roblox experience — the named stores a game creates with DataStoreService:GetDataStore(). Returns each store's name, creation time and state. Reads only; nothing is modified. Use it to find the exact store name before reading or writing an entry. Optionally filter by name prefix and page through results with `pageToken`. This lists stores, not the keys inside them.

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

prefix.description: Only return stores whose name starts with this, e.g. "Player". Case-sensitive.

maxPageSize.description: Stores per page. Roblox defaults to 10 and caps at 100; this tool asks for 100.

pageToken.description: Continue a previous listing. Every other argument must match the call that produced it.

includeDeleted.description: Also list stores that are soft-deleted and awaiting permanent removal.

tools.name: get_data_store_entry
tools.description: Read one entry from a standard data store in a Roblox experience — the saved value for a single key, e.g. one player's profile. Returns the stored JSON value plus its version (revision id), attributes, associated user IDs and state. Reads only; nothing is modified, and the result is not cached, so it reflects what is stored right now. The revision id it returns is what you pass to set_data_store_entry as `matchVersion` to make a safe read-modify-write. Optionally read a past revision instead of the current value.

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

dataStore.description: Exact name of the data store, e.g. "PlayerSaves". Case-sensitive and not fuzzy-matched — call list_data_stores first if you are not certain of the name.

key.description: The entry key inside the data store, e.g. "player_42" or "Player_1234567". 1-50 characters. Case-sensitive and exact.

scope.description: Data store scope. Omit for the default scope ("global" — what Luau uses unless the game passes a scope). Only set this if the game deliberately writes to a named scope.

revision.description: Read a specific past revision id instead of the current value. Also accepts "latest:2024-12-02T06:00:00Z" to read whatever was current at that timestamp.

tools.name: set_data_store_entry
tools.description: Write the value of ONE key in ONE standard data store of a Roblox experience — this replaces that player's saved data. Uses the legacy /datastores/v1 endpoint deliberately, because it is the only Roblox endpoint with a real compare-and-set: `mode: "createOnly"` writes only if the key does not exist, and `mode: "ifVersion"` writes only if the stored version still matches the `matchVersion` you pass (get it from get_data_store_entry). The default `mode: "overwrite"` is unconditional and can silently destroy a write a live game server made a moment earlier — prefer "ifVersion" for anything a running game touches. The value is arbitrary JSON (object, array, string, number, boolean or null), not a string. The entry's attributes and associated user IDs are read first and carried forward automatically, because this endpoint clears them otherwise. Warning: an unrecognised `dataStore` name creates a brand-new data store rather than failing. (Roblox marks this endpoint beta; it may change.)

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

dataStore.description: Exact name of the data store, e.g. "PlayerSaves". Case-sensitive and not fuzzy-matched — call list_data_stores first if you are not certain of the name.

key.description: The entry key inside the data store, e.g. "player_42" or "Player_1234567". 1-50 characters. Case-sensitive and exact.

scope.description: Data store scope. Omit for the default scope ("global" — what Luau uses unless the game passes a scope). Only set this if the game deliberately writes to a named scope.

value.description: The new value, as arbitrary JSON — an object, array, string, number, boolean or null. Pass the value itself, not a JSON string of it. This REPLACES the stored value entirely; to change one field, read the entry first, edit the object and send the whole thing back.

attributes.description: Entry attributes. Omit to keep whatever is already stored — the existing values are read and carried forward. Passing an object REPLACES all attributes.

userIds.description: Roblox user IDs associated with this entry, used for GDPR-style data requests. Omit to keep the stored list. Passing an array REPLACES it.

clearMetadata.description: Set true to deliberately wipe this entry's attributes and user IDs rather than preserving them. Only set this when erasing them is the intent.

mode.description: overwrite — write unconditionally (last writer wins; can lose a concurrent write from a live server). createOnly — write only if the key does not already exist; fails if it does. ifVersion — write only if the stored version still equals `matchVersion`; fails if anything changed since you read it. Use "ifVersion" whenever a live game may be writing this key.

matchVersion.description: Required when mode is "ifVersion". The version the entry must still be at — use the `revisionId` from get_data_store_entry, or the `version` returned by a previous set_data_store_entry call.

tools.name: increment_data_store_entry
tools.description: Atomically add a whole number to the numeric value of ONE key in ONE standard data store of a Roblox experience — for currency, scores and counters. Pass a negative `amount` to subtract. This is safer than read-then-write for counters because Roblox applies it atomically, so it cannot lose a concurrent increment from a live game server. It FAILS if the stored value is not a number, and it CREATES the key (starting from the amount) if it does not exist — so a typo in `key` fabricates player data instead of erroring. Any attributes and user IDs on the entry are cleared unless you re-supply them here.

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

dataStore.description: Exact name of the data store, e.g. "PlayerSaves". Case-sensitive and not fuzzy-matched — call list_data_stores first if you are not certain of the name.

key.description: The entry key inside the data store, e.g. "player_42" or "Player_1234567". 1-50 characters. Case-sensitive and exact.

scope.description: Data store scope. Omit for the default scope ("global" — what Luau uses unless the game passes a scope). Only set this if the game deliberately writes to a named scope.

amount.description: Whole number to add. Negative subtracts. Both the stored value and this must be integers.

users.description: Roblox user IDs to associate with the entry. Roblox CLEARS the existing list if this is omitted, so re-send whatever get_data_store_entry showed if you want to keep it.

attributes.description: Arbitrary metadata map. Roblox CLEARS existing attributes if this is omitted, so re-send what get_data_store_entry showed if you want to keep them.

Read this before changing anything, since an update is live for players immediately and Roblox’s update call returns no body to compare against. (Roblox marks this endpoint beta; it may change.)

tools.name: get_user
tools.description: Look up one Roblox user by numeric user ID: username, display name, join date, bio, locale, Premium status, and — when the API key carries the optional `user.advanced:read` / `user.social:read` permissions — ID-verification status and linked off-platform social profiles. PERSONAL DATA: `idVerified` reflects government-ID or non-VoIP-phone verification, `socialNetworkProfiles` are real off-platform identities, `about` is user-authored text and `locale` is a location signal. Report only what the user actually asked for and do not compile a profile of someone across tools. A missing `idVerified` means "not authorized to see it", never "false". There is no username lookup: pass the numeric ID.

userId.description: The target Roblox user ID (numeric, e.g. 156). This API takes IDs only — there is no username-to-ID lookup anywhere in the API-key Open Cloud surface, so resolve a username to an ID yourself (e.g. from the Roblox website) before calling.

tools.name: list_bans
tools.description: List the user restrictions (bans) recorded for an experience, or for one place inside it. Roblox returns everyone who has EVER been restricted, so check the "State" column: rows where it reads "not banned" are lifted bans that remain on the record. "Duration" of "permanent" means the ban never expires. Includes the moderator-only private reason, so treat the output as internal. (Roblox marks this endpoint beta; it may change.)

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

placeId.description: Optional place ID to scope to a single place. Omit for the whole experience (every place in the universe), which is what "banned from the game" normally means.

maxPageSize.description: Rows per page, 1–100. Roblox defaults to 10, which is usually too few.

tools.name: get_ban_history
tools.description: The moderation audit trail for an experience: every ban and unban, who performed it, when, for how long, and both reasons. Covers universe-level and place-level changes (the place column is empty for experience-wide ones). Filter by `userId` to answer "what happened to this player?". INTERNAL DATA: rows carry moderator identities and the private moderator note, neither of which the affected player has ever seen — do not repeat them to a player or paste them anywhere public. (Roblox marks this endpoint beta; it may change.)

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

userId.description: Only show actions against this numeric user ID.

placeId.description: Optional place ID to scope to a single place. Omit for the whole experience (every place in the universe), which is what "banned from the game" normally means.

maxPageSize.description: Rows per page, 1–100. Roblox defaults to 10, which is usually too few.

tools.name: unban_user
tools.description: Lift a ban: the user can join the experience (or place) again. This is the same Roblox endpoint as `ban_user` with the switch off, and it is the safe direction — it restores access rather than removing it. The restriction record stays in `list_bans` with its state set to inactive, and the unban is written to `get_ban_history`. If a place-level unban appears not to work, the ban is probably inherited from the experience level: omit `placeId` to lift it there. Roblox allows only 2 restriction updates per minute for the same user in the same experience. (Roblox marks this endpoint beta; it may change.)

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

userId.description: The target Roblox user ID (numeric, e.g. 156). This API takes IDs only — there is no username-to-ID lookup anywhere in the API-key Open Cloud surface, so resolve a username to an ID yourself (e.g. from the Roblox website) before calling.

placeId.description: Optional place ID to scope to a single place. Omit for the whole experience (every place in the universe), which is what "banned from the game" normally means.

tools.name: list_experiments
tools.description: List the A/B experiments configured for an experience, with their state (draft, scheduled, running, completed, cancelled, deleted), how much of the audience is exposed, the goal metric and the config key being varied. Read-only: this tool never starts, schedules, updates or completes an experiment, because each of those changes what live players experience. Note there are no results in this API — see `get_experiment_stats`. (Roblox marks this endpoint experimental; it may change.)

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

state.description: Only experiments in this state. Omit for all of them.

search.description: Substring match against the experiment name.

skip.description: Offset-based pagination (this endpoint uses skip/limit, not a page token).

tools.name: get_experiment_stats
tools.description: Diagnostic health check for one experiment. Roblox returns exactly one signal here: `isSrmDetected` — whether a Sample Ratio Mismatch was found, meaning the observed traffic split does not match the configured variant weights, which invalidates the test. There are NO lift, p-value, confidence-interval or per-variant metric numbers anywhere in this API, so do not present this as "the results" — read those on the Creator Dashboard. The response is computed asynchronously: `done: false` means it is not ready yet, so call again shortly. (Roblox marks this endpoint experimental; it may change.)

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

tools.name: upload_asset
tools.description: Upload an image, model, audio or video file from this machine to Roblox as an asset, and wait for Roblox to finish processing it. Returns the new asset ID and, crucially, the moderation state — Roblox reviews every upload, so a finished upload can still be Reviewing or Rejected and must not be reported as usable until it is Approved. Hard limit of 20 MB per file. Set `assetId` only to replace the contents of an existing asset: Roblox can replace the content body of Model assets only, and Audio, Decal, Image and Video assets can never be updated — for those, upload a new asset instead. (Roblox marks this endpoint beta; it may change.)

filePath.description: Absolute path to the file on the machine running this server, e.g. "C:/art/banner.png" or "/home/me/models/tree.fbx".

displayName.description: The asset name shown on Roblox. Required when creating.

description.description: Asset description, 1000 characters maximum. Required when creating.

assetType.description: Roblox asset type: Audio, Decal, Image, Model, Video, Mesh or Animation. Inferred from the file extension when omitted (.png/.jpg → Image, .fbx/.glb/.rbxm → Model, .mp3/.wav → Audio, .mp4 → Video). For images the choice is about which id you get back, not what the picture shows: "Image" returns the texture id that `ImageLabel.Image`, `ImageButton.Image` and `Decal.Texture` need, while "Decal" returns a wrapper id that fails silently in those properties. Choose "Decal" only when something specifically requires a Decal asset.

contentType.description: Override the per-part MIME type, e.g. "model/gltf-binary". Rarely needed.

userId.description: Owning Roblox user id. Defaults to the account this server is configured with.

groupId.description: Owning group id. Mutually exclusive with userId.

assetId.description: Set only to replace the contents of an existing asset. Roblox can only replace the content body of Model assets — Audio, Decal, Image and Video assets cannot be updated at all.

expectedPrice.description: Upload fee in Robux you expect to pay. Roblox fails the upload with 400 if the real fee is higher.

assetPrivacy.description: Privacy override, for asset types that support one. Note the lowercase-first spelling.

tools.name: get_asset
tools.description: Look up one Roblox asset by ID: name, description, type, current revision, archived state and — the reason to call this after an upload — its moderation state (Reviewing, Rejected or Approved). An asset that is not Approved is not usable in an experience. (Roblox marks this endpoint beta; it may change.)

readMask.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. "description,displayName". Omit for everything.

tools.name: list_localization_entries
tools.description: Read an experience’s localization table — the source strings and their translations, the same data LocalizationService serves in-game. Answers "what is translated, and into which languages?". One page at a time; pass the returned cursor for more. If `tableId` is omitted it is looked up from the experience, which asks Roblox for the auto-localization table and creates an empty one if the experience has never had a table. (Roblox marks this endpoint experimental; it may change.)

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

tableId.description: The localization table UUID. Looked up from the experience when omitted.

locale.description: Show only this locale’s translations, e.g. "fr-fr". Omit to see every locale side by side.

entryFormat.description: Entry format to list. Roblox defaults to Legacy; use Icu for ICU-formatted strings.

cursor.description: Page cursor from a previous call’s `nextPageCursor`.

tools.name: update_localization_entries
tools.description: Add source strings to an experience’s localization table, or overwrite their translations for one or more locales. Upsert only — this tool has no way to delete an entry or a locale, so an existing translation can be replaced but never removed. Partial success is normal: the result lists every row Roblox refused, alongside those it accepted. (Roblox marks this endpoint experimental; it may change.)

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

tableId.description: The localization table UUID. Looked up from the experience when omitted.

source.description: The source-language text. Together with key and context this identifies the row.

key.description: Developer-chosen key. Leave empty to identify the row by source + context.

context.description: Scope for the key, usually an instance path.

text.description: The translated string for that locale.

translations.description: One entry per locale to add or overwrite.

entries.description: Rows to upsert. An existing source string gains or updates the translations listed.

tools.name: get_experience_thumbnails
tools.description: List the thumbnail images and icon currently shown on an experience’s Roblox store page, with the render state of each — a thumbnail that is Pending, Blocked or InReview is not visible to players. Read-only: reordering, alt text and per-language thumbnails are managed elsewhere.

experience.description: The experience name, as a person would say it — "my gardening game", "Tower Defense". Matched fuzzily against the configured experiences. Omit when only one is configured.

universeId.description: Exact Roblox universe ID. Takes precedence over `experience`.

size.description: Rendered size, e.g. "768x432" (default) or "576x324". Affects the returned image URLs only.

instructions:
Read-only access to a Roblox creator’s experience analytics.

Start with list_experiences to see which games are available, then get_overview for a general "how is it doing" question. Every analytics tool accepts `experience` as a plain name ("my gardening game") — you do not need a universe ID.

Read the `notes:` line of every result and carry its caveats into your answer: which experience was matched, which buckets are still partial, and whether values may be summed. At weekly or coarser granularity, active-user counts are distinct users per bucket and must never be added together.
